instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-351 Designation of paydays; payment methods; earnings statement
figure_or_rule_carried: Two or more fixed paydays per month, not more than 16 days apart (A); employer with principal place of business and centralized payroll outside AZ may pay FLSA-exempt professional/administrative/executive/outside-sales staff and NLRA supervisors once a month (B; not CBA salaries, G). Lag: wages other than overtime/exception pay not exceeding 5 days of labor may be held back (C1); overtime/exception pay no later than 16 days after period end (C3). Payment: currency, negotiable check, direct deposit with written consent (D4), or payroll card where the employee was offered deposit and neither consents nor designates an institution (D5); employer may in its discretion pay by deposit or, absent a designated institution, payroll card (H). Deposit or payroll card: written or electronic statement of earnings and withholdings (E, F) with no content list; one free withdrawal per deposit; payroll-card fee list (F). Violation = petty offense (I). Local copy for the instrument cited by US-AZ-P5-1-004 / US-AZL-002.

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-352 Withholding of wages (deduction authorization)
figure_or_rule_carried: No employer may withhold or divert wages unless (1) required or empowered by state or federal law, (2) prior written authorization from the employee (revocable in writing; revocation does not stop withholding to resolve a debt to the employer or under court order), or (3) reasonable good-faith dispute about wages due, including counterclaim or set-off.

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-353 Payment of wages of discharged employee
figure_or_rule_carried: Discharge: all wages due within 7 working days or the end of the next regular pay period, whichever is sooner (A). Quit: no later than the regular payday for the pay period in which termination occurred; by mail if requested (B). Payment in lawful money by negotiable check/draft/money order redeemable on demand, or deposit at the employee's financial institution (C). No accrued-vacation payout rule in the section. Violation = petty offense (D).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-362 (L97 ch.51) Minimum wage; prohibition on local minimum wage above federal
figure_or_rule_carried: Text served by azleg.gov for 23-362: no political subdivision may establish a minimum wage above the federal minimum wage (29 USC 206). CONFLICT: the later voter-approved 23-364(I) (Prop. 202, protected by Prop. 105) lets a county, city or town regulate minimum wages by ordinance, not below the state rate; Tucson and Flagstaff operate local rates. The page shows only the 1997 legislative version; the Prop. 202 definitions version of 23-362 (employer/employee) was not served. Build rule: local minimum wages valid under 23-364(I); flag for counsel.

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-363 Minimum wage (Fair Wages and Healthy Families Act, Prop. 206 of 2016)
figure_or_rule_carried: Statutory steps 10.00 (2017), 10.50 (2018), 11.00 (2019), 12.00 (2020) (A). From 2021-01-01 increased each 1 January by the August-over-August percentage change of CPI-U (US city average, all items), the increase rounded to the nearest multiple of 5 cents (B). Tipped employees: up to 3.00/hour below the minimum wage if records of charged tips or FICA tip declarations show tips + wages >= minimum wage each week, averaged over the payroll period (C). The statute carries no 2026/2027 figure; ICA publishes it (ACCESS gap).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-364 Enforcement (records, posting, hire notice, local minimum wages)
figure_or_rule_carried: Post ICA-format notices; give business name, address and telephone number in writing at hire; keep payroll records of hours worked each day and wages and earned paid sick time paid for 4 years (failure = rebuttable presumption of underpayment); employee may inspect and copy own payroll records (D). Civil penalty at least 250 first, at least 1,000 subsequent/willful (F). Underpayment: balance + interest + twice the underpaid amount (G). Counties, cities and towns may set higher minimum wages and benefits by ordinance (I).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-371 Earned paid sick time - definitions
figure_or_rule_carried: Earned paid sick time is paid at the same hourly rate and with the same benefits the employee normally earns, never below the FLSA or state minimum wage (D). Employer covers private entities and political subdivisions, but not the State of Arizona or the United States (G). Year = regular consecutive 12-month period chosen by the employer (L).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-372 Accrual of earned paid sick time
figure_or_rule_carried: Accrual 1 hour per 30 hours worked. Annual accrual/use cap 40 hours (15+ employees) or 24 hours (<15 employees) unless the employer sets higher (A, B). Headcount counts full-time, part-time and temporary; 15+ on payroll in 20 calendar weeks of the current or preceding year (C). Accrual from hire; 90-day use wait allowed (D1-2). FLSA-exempt employees assumed to work 40 h/week (D3). Carry-over required, or pay unused time at year end and front-load (D4). Rehire within 9 months reinstates the balance (D5); successor employer carries balances (D6). An equivalent PTO policy satisfies the article (E). No payout of unused time on separation required (F).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-373 Use of earned paid sick time
figure_or_rule_carried: Uses: own or family illness, care and preventive care; public-health closure of the workplace or of a child's school/care; domestic violence, sexual violence, abuse or stalking (A). Smallest increment = the smaller of one hour or the smallest increment the payroll system uses for absences (F). Documentation only for 3+ consecutive work days (G).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-377 Confidentiality of earned paid sick time information (with 23-374)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer may not require disclosure of health or domestic-violence details to grant sick time; such information is confidential and disclosed only to the employee or with the employee's permission. 23-374: anti-retaliation; absence-control policies may not count earned paid sick time (C).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-375(C) Earned paid sick time balances on the paycheck
figure_or_rule_carried: MANDATORY PAY-STATEMENT CONTENT: the amount of earned paid sick time available, the amount taken to date in the year, and the amount of pay received as earned paid sick time shall be recorded in, or on an attachment to, the employee's regular paycheck. Same instrument as US-AZL-001 (which carries subsection B, notice language); this row carries subsection C. Not a supersession.

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-722.01 New hire reporting
figure_or_rule_carried: Report to DES every hire, rehire or return to work (after layoff, furlough, separation, leave without pay or termination) of an employee who resides or works in AZ (A). Form: W-4 or equivalent; magnetic, electronic, first-class mail or fax (C). Deadline 20 days after hire/rehire/return; electronic filers in two monthly transmissions not more than 16 days apart (D). Fields: employee name, address, SSN; employer name, address, FEIN; date the employee first performed services for pay (D). Multistate employers may designate one state and notify HHS (E). No employer penalty for non-reporting (K).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-233 Hours of labor for persons under 16
figure_or_rule_carried: Under 16: max 40 h/week and 8 h/day when school is not in session; 18 h/week and 3 h/day when in session; no night work (from 9:30 pm before a school day, 11:00 pm otherwise, until 6:00 am); newspaper delivery exempt.

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-617 Exempt employment (Arizona UI)
figure_or_rule_carried: Excluded from UI employment: agricultural labor unless the employer had 10+ ag workers in 20 weeks or paid 20,000+ cash ag wages in a quarter (1); service for own son/daughter/spouse and by a child under 21 for a parent (4); federal service (5); students employed by their school and student spouses in aid programs (9); religious/charitable/educational 501(c)(3)-type organizations, subject to 23-615 exceptions (10); student nurses and interns (11); commission-only insurance, real estate, securities and tax-preparer salespersons (12, 14, 19, 23); under-18 newspaper delivery (13); foreign governments (15-16); casual labor outside trade or business (18); co-op students in credit programs (20); hospital patients (21); direct sellers (22).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 23-615 Employment (Arizona UI) - religious exclusions
figure_or_rule_carried: Excludes from UI employment service for a church, convention or association of churches or a primarily religious organization operated, supervised, controlled or principally supported by a church, and service by a duly ordained, commissioned or licensed minister in the exercise of the ministry or by a member of a religious order performing required duties. Domestic-service coverage threshold not extracted in this pass.

instrument_name: A.R.S. 33-1131 Exempt earnings (creditor garnishment and support limits)
figure_or_rule_carried: Creditor garnishment: the maximum subject to process per workweek is the LESSER of 10 percent of disposable earnings or the amount by which disposable earnings exceed 60 times the highest applicable (federal, state or local) minimum hourly wage (B) - stricter than CCPA (25 percent / 30x federal minimum). Support orders: one-half of disposable earnings per pay period exempt (C) (CCPA allows 50-65 percent). Exemptions do not apply to bankruptcy chapter XIII orders or state/federal tax debts (D). Disposable earnings include bonuses, commissions and pension/deferred compensation, after legally required withholding (A). The page shows no effective date for the 10 percent text (Prop. 209, Nov 2022, lead only): effective_from left blank.

instrument_name: A.R.S. 12-1598.10 Continuing lien on earnings (wage garnishment procedure)
figure_or_rule_carried: Earnings garnishment is a continuing lien on nonexempt earnings; it ends when the judgment is satisfied, vacated or expires, the debtor leaves employment for more than 60 days (90 for school-year contracts), the creditor releases, a stay, no nonexempt earnings for 60 days, or the court quashes (D). Subsection (F) still refers to a 25 percent maximum under 33-1131(B), reducible to 15 percent for hardship, while 33-1131(B) now reads 10 percent: statutory text inconsistency (open question).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 25-504 Order of assignment for support (Arizona income withholding)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer begins withholding no later than 14 days after receipt (E); ex parte order: first employer waits 14 calendar days and serves a copy on the employee within 5 days (F). Remit to the support payment clearinghouse within 2 business days after the obligor is paid; 25-510 handling fee deducted and transmitted monthly; employer cost fee 1 USD per payment, max 4 USD per month per obligor; combined remittances identify each obligor by SSN; notify end of employment and new employer within 10 days; order revives on rehire within 90 days (H). Priority over all other executions, attachments or garnishments; current child support met first; 33-1131 exemption applies (P).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 44-1373 Restricted use of social security numbers
figure_or_rule_carried: No person may intentionally make an individual's SSN available to the general public, print it on a card needed to obtain services, require its internet transmission unless secure or encrypted, or require it to access a website without a password/PIN (A). Collection and use required by state/federal law or for internal verification is permitted (C). No AZ statute read requires SSN truncation on the pay statement; ADOR Pub 701 forbids truncating SSNs on W-2s filed with ADOR [US-AZS5-025].

instrument_name: A.R.S. 43-401 Withholding tax; rates; election by employee (local copy)
figure_or_rule_carried: Withholding on wages, salary, bonus or other emolument for services in AZ per department tables (A): bonuses take the same elected percentage (no separate supplemental rate located). Employer may elect not to withhold in December, notifying ADOR and employees before 1 July (B, F). Employee elects within 5 days of employment on the ADOR form; otherwise the department default percentage applies (E). Employer may reduce withholding for designated tax-credit contributions (Form A-4C), remit the reduction to the organization within 15 days after quarter end and give the employee a statement within 30 days after year end or 15 days after termination (G). No withholding for nonresident disaster-recovery workers (H). Subsection C (reconciliation), cited by 43-412, is not printed on the served page. Local copy for US-AZ-P5-1-003.

instrument_name: A.R.S. 43-403 Employment excluded from withholding
figure_or_rule_carried: No withholding on: nonresident common-carrier employees working in and outside AZ; domestic service in a private home; casual labor outside trade or business; part-time/seasonal hand agricultural labor (machine operators excepted); nonresidents present under 60 days in the calendar year for an employer with AZ property, payroll and sales (days in transit, personal, unrelated training excluded); nonresident disaster-recovery workers (A). Motion-picture nonresident exemption on application (B). The 60-day rule does not cover athletes/entertainers (C). Nonresident and seasonal agricultural employees may elect withholding; employer may withhold before day 60 (D).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 43-412 Returns of withholding (annual return due 31 January)
figure_or_rule_carried: With the reconciliation the employer files a return of total wages and amounts deducted (A). Annual return summarizing total compensation and tax withheld per employee, due on or before 31 January of the following year, extendable for good cause, under penalties of perjury (B).

instrument_name: A.R.S. 43-105 Internal Revenue Code conformity date
figure_or_rule_carried: For taxable years beginning after 2025-12-31, IRC = the Code in effect on 2026-01-01 including retroactive 2025 provisions, excluding later changes (A). AZ withholding base = federal wages; amounts excluded from federal wages are excluded from AZ withholding [US-AZS5-024]: federal exclusions (401(k) deferrals, section 125, HSA, transit, group-term life within limits) carry over for withholding; no AZ departure located in this pass (Form 140 additions/subtractions not read).

instrument_name: ADOR Withholding Tax page (live copy 2026-11-02)
figure_or_rule_carried: Withholding = percentage of gross taxable wages = federal wages (IRC 3401, generally W-2 box 1); amounts excluded from federal wages and federal mandatory withholding are excluded from AZ withholding. Options 0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0/2.5/3.0/3.5 percent. New employee completes Form A-4 within 5 days, else 2.0 percent until a different election; extra amount allowed; zero-percent election renewed annually. Resident physically working in AZ: withhold from the start regardless of employer location; AZ resident working outside AZ may request withholding on Form A-4V; nonresident in AZ: after 60 days, earlier by agreement. Form WEC exemptions: Native Americans living and working on their own reservation, military spouses (MSRRA), residents of CA, IN, OR, VA claiming the credit. Rules A.A.C. R15-2B-101, R15-2B-102. Fresh live read of the page held by US-AZ-P5-1-002 (Wayback 2026-10-09); same content.

instrument_name: ADOR Pub 701 Submitting Forms A1-R/A1-APR and W-2, W-2c, W-2G, 1099 (rev. Jan 2025)
figure_or_rule_carried: A1-R / A1-APR must be filed electronically (A.R.S. 43-323(F)): AZFSET bulk .csv upload, AZTaxes data entry, or registered transmitter; Form 292 waiver. State copies of W-2/W-2c reporting AZ wages or AZ withholding, and W-2G/1099 reporting AZ withholding, are mandatory electronic attachments due with the reconciliation (31 January or extended date), .txt upload via AZTaxes or AZFSET. Layout follows SSA EFW2 (Pub 42-007) with exceptions: RS (State) record required for each employee, RV optional, Arizona state code 04; 1099: IRS Pub 1220 Payee B record, one form type per file, filed directly with ADOR despite CF/SF. Do not truncate SSNs or EINs. Optical media (CD/DVD/flash) only for attachments, with Form A1-T. Text speaks of calendar year 2024; no 2026 edition located (live URL 403, Wayback copy read).

instrument_name: BLS CPI-U US city average, all items (CUUR0000SA0), August values
figure_or_rule_carried: CPI-U NSA, US city average: August 2024 = 314.796; August 2025 = 323.976; August 2026 = 334.980. August-over-August: 2025 +2.9162 percent (drives 1 Jan 2026); 2026 +3.3965 percent (drives 1 Jan 2027). Caliber named by A.R.S. 23-363(B) and by the Tucson Minimum Wage Act.

instrument_name: City of Tucson - Tucson Minimum Wage Act page (Prop. 206 of 2021)
authority: City of Tucson, Business Services Department (Labor Standards Unit)
figure_or_rule_carried: Tucson minimum wage 15.45 USD/hour from 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31; 16.00 USD/hour from 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31; indexed yearly by CPI-U and rises to any higher state/federal rate. Applies to employees with at least 5 hours of work per pay cycle within city limits; not to the State of Arizona, the US or tribal entities; casual babysitting at the employer's home excluded. Tip credit max 3.00 USD. History: 13.00 (2022-04-01); 2023 and 2024 paid at the state rate, 13.85 and 14.35, under A.R.S. 23-363(B); 15.00 (2025). G-DERIVE: 15.00 x 1.029162 = 15.4374 -> 15.45; 15.45 x 1.033965 = 15.9748 -> 16.00 (nearest 0.05).
